current.jp: 高校生はこの試合に出られない
current.kana: こうこうせいわこのしあいにでられない

structure_explanation.en: The topic 高校生は ('as for high schoolers') is marked by は. The target この試合に ('in this game') is marked by に, the particle that with 出る ('to go out, to enter/take part in an event') indicates what one takes part in. The verb is in the negative potential form 出られない ('cannot take part'): 出る becomes 出られる (to be able to) and ない negates it.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico 高校生は ('quanto aos colegiais') é marcado por は. O alvo この試合に ('neste jogo') é marcado por に, partícula que com 出る ('sair, entrar/participar de um evento') indica aquilo de que se participa. O verbo está na forma potencial negativa 出られない ('não pode participar'): 出る vira 出られる (poder) e ない o nega.

translation_literal.en: As for the high school student, in this match he cannot take part.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao colegial, neste jogo não consegue/pode sair (participar).

translation.en: High school students can't take part in this game.
translation.pt-BR: Estudantes do ensino médio não podem participar deste jogo.

gloss.en: to go out; here: take part / enter (the game)

note.en: stem 出 of 出る, base for the potential form 出られる
note.pt-BR: raiz 出 de 出る, base para a forma potencial 出られる

note.en: auxiliary られる that forms the potential of 出る (出られる = 'to be able to take part')
note.pt-BR: auxiliar られる que forma o potencial de 出る (出られる = 'poder participar')

note.en: ない negating 出られる, resulting in 出られない ('cannot take part')
note.pt-BR: ない negando 出られる, resultando em 出られない ('não poder participar')

objections.objection: Pre-existing and untouched by the ops, but it ships in 'after': the token array contains 高校 (こうこう) and 生 (せい) as glossless tokens AND 高校生 (こうこうせい) as a third, fully glossed token. Concatenating token readings yields こうこうせいこうこうせいわ…, which does not match the kana field こうこうせいわこのしあいにでられない, so any furigana/kana reconstruction from tokens is wrong. No other record in the batch carries both the parts and the whole (cf. 県/下 with no 県下 token, お/土産 with no お土産 token).
objections.auditor_hint: Drop tokens[0] (高校) and tokens[1] (生), keep only the 高校生 token, and renumber i from 0.

current.jp: 土曜日または日曜日に行きます
current.kana: どようびまたわにちようびにいきます

structure_explanation.en: Two day options (土曜日 'Saturday' and 日曜日 'Sunday') are joined by または ('or,' the exercise focus). The particle に marks the time of the action ('on [day]'), and 行きます is 'to go' in the polite form. Note that に comes only after the whole expression 'A または B,' covering both options.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Duas opções de dia (土曜日 'sábado' e 日曜日 'domingo') são unidas por または ('ou', foco do exercício). A partícula に marca o momento da ação ('em/no [dia]'), e 行きます é 'ir' na forma educada. Note que に vem só depois de toda a expressão 'A または B', cobrindo as duas opções.

translation_literal.en: On Saturday or Sunday, I'll go.

translation.en: I'll go on Saturday or Sunday.
translation.pt-BR: Vou no sábado ou no domingo.

note.en: connective form (行き) of 行く, linking to ます
note.pt-BR: forma conectiva (行き) de 行く, ligando-se a ます

note.en: ます in the polite affirmative present
note.pt-BR: ます no presente afirmativo educado

objections.objection: Token stream does not reconstruct the sentence and ships in after: tokens 0-3 are 土曜=どよう / 日=び / 日曜=にちよう / 日=び, duplicating words that then appear again as tokens 4 and 7 (土曜日=どようび, 日曜日=にちようび), and the duplicate 日曜 sub-token even precedes 土曜日. Concatenating token readings yields どようびにちようびどようびまたわにちようびにいきます, which does not match kana どようびまたわにちようびにいきます. Every other record in the batch concatenates exactly. This is a tokenizer merge artifact (the four leading tokens carry null gloss/role/note) that makes the learner see each weekday twice.
objections.auditor_hint: Drop the four duplicate sub-tokens (indices 0-3) and re-index, leaving 土曜日 / また / は / 日曜日 / に / 行き / ます.

current.jp: 朝の光がとても明るいです
current.kana: あさのひかりがとてもあかるいです

structure_explanation.en: The sentence follows the pattern [subject + が + adverb + い-adjective + です]. 朝の光 (the morning light) is the subject, marked by が. とても (very) intensifies the adjective 明るい (bright), and です gives a polite tone without changing the adjective.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase segue o padrão [sujeito + が + advérbio + adjetivo-い + です]. 朝の光 (a luz da manhã) é o sujeito, marcado por が. とても (muito) intensifica o adjetivo 明るい (claro/brilhante), e です dá tom educado, sem mudar o adjetivo.

translation_literal.en: The morning light is very bright.
translation_literal.pt-BR: A luz da manhã é muito clara.

translation.en: The morning light is very bright.
translation.pt-BR: A luz da manhã é muito clara.

note.en: dictionary form (present) of 明るい, an い-adjective
note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (presente) de 明るい, adjetivo-い

note.en: です after an い-adjective only for a polite tone
note.pt-BR: です após adjetivo-い apenas para tom educado

objections.objection: Over-corrected. Removing the wrong は-topic device was right, but the replacement is byte-identical to translation.en ("The morning light is very bright.") and translation.pt-BR ("A luz da manhã é muito clara."). translation_literal now duplicates the natural translation in BOTH locales and no longer mirrors the Japanese structure at all, so the field loses its function and the learner sees the same line twice. Every sibling fix of this same defect class in this batch kept a structural mirror instead (29ba9e17cab1 kept the "(em)" に marker; 31530346515a kept "(obj.)"; 2fc442bf040c kept the fronted scope phrase; 2eeb7996105f kept "cai e tal, para e tal, está fazendo"). The が subject should simply be rendered plainly with its role marked, not erased.
objections.auditor_hint: pt-BR: "A luz da manhã (sujeito), muito clara é." / en: "The morning light (subject) is very bright."

current.jp: この山の高さに驚いた
current.kana: このやまのたかさにおどろいた

structure_explanation.en: The target is the suffix さ, which turns adjectives into nouns of degree/measure: 高い (tall/high) becomes 高さ (height). Here 高さ is the noun that takes the particle に, indicating what caused the surprise. The structure is [この山の高さ] (the height of this mountain) + に + 驚いた (I was surprised). The subject 'I' is understood, and the verb is in the past.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O alvo é o sufixo さ, que transforma adjetivos em substantivos de grau/medida: 高い (alto) vira 高さ (altura). Aqui 高さ é o substantivo que recebe a partícula に, indicando aquilo que causou a surpresa. A estrutura é [この山の高さ] (a altura desta montanha) + に + 驚いた (surpreendi-me). O sujeito 'eu' fica subentendido, e o verbo está no passado.

translation_literal.en: As for this mountain's height, I was surprised by it.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à altura desta montanha, (eu) me surpreendi com (に) ela.

translation.en: I was struck by how tall this mountain is.
translation.pt-BR: Fiquei impressionado com a altura desta montanha.

note.en: nominalization of 高い (tall/high) with the suffix さ → 高さ (height)
note.pt-BR: nominalização de 高い (alto) com o sufixo さ → 高さ (altura)

gloss.en: to be surprised / to be impressed

note.en: stem of the past form of 驚く (驚い + た)
note.pt-BR: radical da forma passada de 驚く (驚い + た)

note.en: auxiliary た that forms the past of 驚く
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た que forma o passado de 驚く

objections.objection: Same topic-device violation, left untouched. jp この山の高さに驚いた has no は; 高さ is marked by に (cause/stimulus), exactly as the record's own structure_explanation states ("高さ é o substantivo que recebe a partícula に, indicando aquilo que causou a surpresa"). But lit_pt opens "Quanto à altura desta montanha," and lit_en "As for this mountain's height," applying the は-only device to a に adjunct. The literal fields therefore contradict the explanation in the same record.
objections.auditor_hint: pt-BR: "Com a altura desta montanha (に), (eu) me surpreendi." / en: "At this mountain's height (に), I was surprised."

current.jp: スプーンが一本足りない
current.kana: すぷーんがいっぽんたりない

structure_explanation.en: The subject スプーン is marked by が because it introduces new information (something that is lacking). 一本 is the number one with the counter 本, used for long, thin objects like cutlery. The verb 足りない is the negative form of 足りる ('to be enough'), so 'is not enough' is equivalent, in natural English, to 'is missing'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O sujeito スプーン é marcado por が porque introduz uma informação nova (algo que falta). 一本 é o número um com o contador 本, usado para objetos longos e finos como talheres. O verbo 足りない é a forma negativa de 足りる ('ser suficiente'), então 'não é suficiente' equivale, em pt-BR natural, a 'está faltando'.

translation_literal.en: As for spoons, one isn't enough.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a colher, uma unidade (long.), não basta/falta.

gloss.en: counter for long thin objects (here: -hon → 本/ぽん)
gloss.pt-BR: contador para objetos longos e finos (aqui: -hon → 本/ぽん)

note.en: stem of 足りる attached to the negation auxiliary ない
note.pt-BR: radical de 足りる ligado ao auxiliar de negação ない

note.en: auxiliary that negates 足りる, forming 足りない ('is not enough')
note.pt-BR: auxiliar que nega 足りる, formando 足りない ('não basta')

objections.objection: Ships a topic-device violation that this same batch treats as major elsewhere. jp スプーンが一本足りない contains no は at all: スプーン is marked by the subject particle が. Yet lit_pt reads "Quanto a colher, uma unidade (long.), não basta/falta." and lit_en "As for spoons, one isn't enough." The "Quanto a X / As for X" device mirrors は only. Unchanged by the patch, while the identical defect was fixed as major in five sibling records in this very file (29ba9e17cab1, 2ac1da0599a1, 2eeb7996105f, 2fc442bf040c, 31530346515a) - shipping both states teaches contradictory rules. Secondary: "Quanto a colher" is also ungrammatical pt-BR (bare noun with no article after "quanto a").
objections.auditor_hint: pt-BR: "Colher (sujeito), uma unidade (contador long.), não basta." / en: "Spoon (subject), one (long-object counter), isn't enough."
